In class five, Ishita got stuck on the word "environment" while reading aloud. Her tongue tied itself, and a hot flush crept up her neck. She wobbled her head like a broken toy and pulled her mouth into a wide, silly shape. The class roared, and Gurpreet Ma'am bit back a smile before asking her to try again. Ishita grinned and bowed to the class, but under the desk she was twisting her hem into a knot.
At fifteen, Ishita came out of the last period and dropped her bag on the bench. "Ugh." Jomon, waiting for her, frowned. "Was that at me?" Ishita blinked, then realised how it had sounded. "No, no. Sorry. Ugh, what a draining day. Two tests and a fight with the printer." Jomon relaxed and held out half his samosa. "Should've said so." Ishita bit into it, laughing. From then on, when a day went badly, she tried to put a few words after the sound so nobody had to guess.

qa.q: Which word did Ishita stumble on while reading aloud in class five?
qa.a: She got stuck on the word "environment".

qa.q: How are the silly face at ten and the "Ugh" at fifteen alike, and how did Ishita change?
qa.a: Both are quick ways to control a moment: at ten Ishita wobbled her head and pulled her mouth into a silly shape, and at fifteen she said Ugh. When Jomon asked if it was at him, she put a few words after the sound so nobody had to guess.

qa.q: What was Ishita feeling when she grinned and bowed but twisted her hem into a knot?
qa.a: She was embarrassed and worried underneath, and the clowning helped her stay in control of the moment.

qa.q: What could Jomon do when someone's short sound leaves him unsure?
qa.a: He can ask calmly, as he did with "Was that at me?", and then listen to the answer without taking offence.

grounding: A class clown's joke covering embarrassment (3891) and a teen's 'ugh' that is softened with a few words (2527): both are ways to manage a feeling, at different ages.
